title: Galba
lead: Servius Sulpicius Galba, emperor from Nero's fall until he was killed in the Forum on 15 January AD 69. Tacitus says that by everyone's agreement he would have been judged fit to rule if he had never ruled (Histories of Tacitus 1:49).

sections.b:
Tacitus gives him an old noble family, a middling mind, a name for fighting in Germany, and fair government in Africa and Nearer Spain (1:49). He was old, he would not pay the soldiers the bonus promised in his name, and Titus Vinius, Cornelius Laco and the freedman Icelus ran his court (1:5-7, 1:13). His adoption of Piso on 10 January was meant to calm the empire and instead let Otho strike (1:14-19).

Josephus mentions him in one line: Galba was slain in the middle of the market place after reigning seven months and seven days (Jewish War 4.9.2). Suetonius says he died in his seventy-third year and the seventh month of his reign (Galba 23). The Wikipedia page gives his birth as 24 December 3 BC, which would make him about 70, and notes that Suetonius and Tacitus have him in his 73rd year.
sections.refs: Histories of Tacitus 1:5-7; Histories of Tacitus 1:13-19; Histories of Tacitus 1:49

sections.h: A link to the New Testament?
sections.b: Galba is not named in the Bible. His reign falls between Nero (whom the New Testament never names, only as Caesar, Acts 25:11-12) and the Flavian emperors who ended the Jewish war. Some readers count his short reign among the "seven kings" of Revelation 17:10; the site's note on that verse sets out the counts.
